speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: asked the Minister for National Development (a) for each year over the past five years, how many pet animal abandonment cases have been investigated; (b) how many fines and jail terms have been issued; (c) what proportion of these animals are cats; and (d) whether the Ministry will review and strengthen frameworks for investigations into and sentencing for such cases.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: We take a serious view of pet abandonment, and all acts involving failure in the duty of care for pets.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: NParks investigates all feedback on alleged pet abandonment and will take enforcement action as appropriate.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Individuals who are found guilty of pet abandonment can be charged under the Animals and Birds Act.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Could I follow up quickly on whether we would consider micro-chipping the cats?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This is something I have pushed for for many years because I think that will help to reduce the abandonment of cats, as for example, like dogs that we now license and micro-chip.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It is pretty hard to abandon them because we would be able to trace the owners quite easily.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: We have undertaken a review and put in place various new practices, guidelines to raise standards of pet care, training, breeding, boarding, as well as the kinds of licensing regimes.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: I think the Minister of State mentioned that penalties are being reviewed.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: I think there is feedback from animal rights, animal rescue groups, that some of the sentences for offences that are being seen are below the maximum and may not be so effective as a deterrent.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Is there a timeframe for this review of the penalties for pet abandonment?

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: As also shared in my reply to Member Mr Louis Ng, we are undertaking – and it is actually in process – quite a comprehensive review of the pet sector.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: We are looking at the various regimes, regulations, guidelines, best practices and engaging various stakeholders.
